abstract: Maintains aerodrome flight approach certifications and instrument landing compliance records
system_message:
You are the Aviation flight operations director (FLTOPS). Your responsibilities include maintaining aerodrome flight approach certifications and instrument landing compliance records, as well as tracking microburst wind shear monitoring data across candidate airfields.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Microburst wind shear monitoring（WIND）
information_points.content:
FLTOPS-WIND-F0L：Terminal weather radar telemetry for Deschutes Ridge Airstrip indicates a Doppler radar update cycle frequency of 6 min for approach corridor wind shear detection sweeps.
FLTOPS-WIND-Y97：At Klamath Basin Airfield, terminal weather radar telemetry records a Doppler radar update cycle frequency of 2 min between automated low-level wind shear hazard sweeps along the approach corridor.
FLTOPS-WIND-04A：Terminal weather radar telemetry for Bitterroot Valley Aerodrome logs a Doppler radar update cycle frequency of 4 min between sweeps detecting low-level wind shear hazards in the approach corridor.

information_points.title: Maintains aerodrome flight approach certifications and instrument landing compliance records（AVCERT）
information_points.content:
FLTOPS-AVCERT-KOX：Deschutes Ridge Airstrip holds active instrument flight rules approach authorization based on its civil aviation aerodrome certification audit. Its Category I precision instrument approach procedure specifies an instrument approach decision height of 75 m above aerodrome elevation.
FLTOPS-AVCERT-4EO：Bitterroot Valley Aerodrome maintains verified instrument flight rules approach authorization in the civil aviation aerodrome certification registry. For Category I precision approaches, its instrument approach decision height is 45 m above aerodrome elevation.
FLTOPS-AVCERT-VSR：Klamath Basin Airfield holds active instrument flight rules approach authorization according to the civil aviation aerodrome certification audit. Its Category I precision instrument approach procedure establishes an instrument approach decision height of 45 m above aerodrome elevation.
